verdicts.claim: SQLite auto-checkpoints when a COMMIT leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more (about 4 MB) or when the last connection closes; the default is PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint=1000
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes'; pragma.html: 'zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off... interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT'

verdicts.claim: All automatic checkpoints and plain sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() calls are PASSIVE. The committing thread runs them, and they never invoke the busy handler.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE' and 'run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT'; C API: 'busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode'

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint modes: PASSIVE ... FULL ... RESTART ... TRUNCATE also truncates the WAL to zero bytes on success. FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE block new writers but not readers
verdicts.evidence: C API: FULL 'blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded'; TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: If the busy handler gives up (returns 0) during a FULL, RESTART or TRUNCATE checkpoint, the call continues as PASSIVE and returns SQLITE_BUSY. PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row
verdicts.evidence: C API: 'If the busy-handler returns 0 ... proceeds ... in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned'; pragma: 'single row with three integer columns ... second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'

verdicts.claim: Cost trade-off: checkpoints need syncs (WAL before copy, database before reset), so they are slower than write transactions ... synchronous=NORMAL the checkpoint is the only operation that syncs
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'WAL must be synced ... prior to moving content ... database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL ... make checkpoints slower than write transactions'; 'with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier ... transactions are no longer durable'

verdicts.claim: For many overlapping readers, the SQLite docs suggest creating reader gaps or running manual RESTART or TRUNCATE checkpoints, which run to completion but may block readers
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'ensuring that there are "reader gaps" ... running manual checkpoints with the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART or SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE option ... readers might block while the checkpoint is running'

verdicts.claim: Litestream's pattern is PASSIVE checkpoints by default (min 1000 pages, 1-minute interval) with a forced TRUNCATE only when the WAL passes truncate-page-n (default 121,359 pages
verdicts.evidence: Litestream: 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000', 'checkpoint-interval: 1m', 'truncate-page-n: 121359 # Default: ~500MB', forced TRUNCATE 'waits for all active writers AND readers', 'truncate-page-n: 0 ... Recommended for Long-Read Apps', 'WAL can grow unbounded'. Nuance omitted: since v0.5.15 Litestream tries PASSIVE first at the threshold and forces TRUNCATE only if that fails.

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation: a checkpoint can only finish and reset the WAL when no other connection is using it. A checkpoint stops at the end mark of any current reader
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader ... will resume ... from where it left off'; 'if there is always at least one active reader ... the WAL file will grow without bound'

verdicts.claim: A completed checkpoint does not shrink the WAL file ... unless PRAGMA journal_size_limit=N is set (... default -1 = no limit) or a TRUNCATE checkpoint runs
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set) ... start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning'; pragma: 'Each time a transaction is committed or a WAL file resets ... truncated to the limit ... default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'

verdicts.claim: A large single write transaction cannot be reset mid-transaction ... Since SQLite 3.11.0 (2016-02-15) the WAL size for one transaction is proportional to the transaction size
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction'; 'As of SQLite version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15), the WAL file for a single transaction should be proportional in size to the transaction itself'
